title: Word 25 — On Love for God
attribution_note: Word 25 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: God, the highest and unchanging Good

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! All Christians say, “How could one not love God!” Or, “Whom should we love, if not God?” True words indeed — how could one not love God, and whom should we love, if not God? God is the highest, uncreated, beginningless, infinite, essential, and unchanging Good. As the sun always shines and fire always warms, so God is Good by nature and always does good, so that “no one is good but God alone” [Matthew 19:17]. God does us good even when He punishes us, for He punishes us in order to correct us; He strikes us in order to have mercy on us; He grieves us in order truly to console us. *“The Lord disciplines the one He loves, and chastises every son whom He receives”* [Hebrews 12:6]. How, then, could one not love such a Good — God?

O most holy, most beloved counsel! God the Trihypostatic — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — said of man, “Let Us make man.” What kind of man? “According to Our image,” He said, “and likeness.” O wondrous goodness of God toward man! O highest honor of humankind! Man was created by God according to the image and likeness of God. What other creature has been deemed worthy of such honor from God? We see no such thing. Man alone was deemed worthy of it, and honored by God with His very image.

O most beloved and most beautiful of God's creations — man! He bears within himself the image of God, like a royal seal. Glorious is the king, and glorious too is his portrait. God, the King of Heaven, is worthy of every honor, and His image, man, is worthy of honor as well. Such goodness, O Christians, did God pour out upon us in creating us. How, then, could we not love Him?

We fell and perished — a thing we can never mourn enough. *“Man, being in honor, did not understand; he was compared to the senseless beasts, and became like them”* [Psalm 48:13]. But the Man-loving God did not abandon us even then: He devised for us a wondrous way of salvation. He sent to us His Only-Begotten Son to save us and bring us back to Himself. *“For God so loved the world that He gave His Only-Begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.* *For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world through Him might be saved”* [John 3:16–17]. How, then, could we not love God, who loves us so? God is the Lover of Mankind, as we all call Him; man too must be a lover of God. For love can be repaid with nothing else but love and gratitude.

God is our Provider; He watches over us and cares for us. He gives us food, clothing, and shelter. His sun, moon, and stars give us light. By His fire we warm ourselves and cook our food. With His water we wash and refresh ourselves. His animals serve us; His air gives us life and sustains it. In a word, we live wrapped in His goodness and love, and without them we could not survive a single moment. How, then, could we not love such a Benefactor — God, who has so loved us? We love a human benefactor; how much more ought we love God our Benefactor! For all creation, and man himself, is God's own wealth: *“The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof”* [Psalm 23:1].

God is our Father. To Him we pray and say, “Our Father, who art in heaven,” and the rest. How, then, could we not love God the Father? Good children always love their father. And if we too wish to be sincere children of God, and to call Him Father without pretense, then we must love Him as our Father. So it is rightly said by all: how could one not love God?

sections.heading: The heart is where love lives

pairs.en: Like every virtue, love must dwell in the heart. When it is not in the heart, in truth it does not exist at all. God does not speak to our lips, saying: love, humble yourself, show mercy, pray, ask, call upon Me, and so on — He speaks to our heart. So we must have love, humility, mercy, prayer, and the rest within the heart. And if it is truly there, it will inevitably show itself outwardly, the way a belch betrays the stomach. For hidden fire reveals itself by warmth, and fragrant balm by its sweet scent. So holy David showed the love he had for God in his most sweet songs to Him: *“I will love You, O Lord, my strength!* *The Lord is my support, my refuge, and my Deliverer, my God, my Helper, in whom I trust, my Protector, and the horn of my salvation, and my Defender”* [Psalm 17:2–3]. Love, though it hides in the heart, cannot remain hidden — it shows its outward signs.

sections.heading: Six signs of true love for God

pairs.en: 1) The Lord Himself points to it, saying, *“He who has My commandments and keeps them, it is he who loves Me”* [John 14:21]. For whoever truly loves God is careful to avoid everything displeasing to Him, and strives to do all that pleases Him, and therefore keeps His holy commandments. From this it follows that those Christians who are careless of His commandments do not have the love of God. Among them are the malicious and all who harm others in any way; fornicators, adulterers, and every kind of defiler; thieves, robbers, plunderers, and all who unjustly seize what belongs to another; slanderers and abusers; the crafty and cunning who deceive others, cheats and hypocrites; sorcerers and those who consult them, and all lawbreakers. None of these love either the law of God or God Himself. They love themselves and their own whims, not God and His holy law.

sections.heading: Joy, contempt for the world, and remembrance

pairs.en: Such a man uses food, drink, clothing, and the rest only out of necessity, never for indulgence. From this it follows that whoever loves the world does not love God, as the apostle testifies: *“If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him”* [1 John 2:15]. Such are those who want to live in the pride and pomp of this world — to live in rich houses, ride in fine carriages, dress in costly clothing, and be praised and honored by all. Such people love *“the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”* [1 John 2:16] — that is, everything contrary to God — and not God.

sections.heading: Remembering God, and never leaving Him

pairs.en: 5) One who loves desires to be inseparable from the one he loves. Many Christians wish to be with Christ the Lord in His glory, but do not wish to be with Him in dishonor and reproach, or to carry the cross. They pray to be in His kingdom, but do not wish to suffer with Him in this world, and thereby show that their heart is not upright, and that they do not truly love Christ — indeed, to tell the truth, they love themselves more than Christ. That is why the Lord says, *“He who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me”* [Matthew 10:38]. A true friend is known in misfortune. He is our true friend, and he truly loves us, who does not abandon us in misfortune. So too, he truly loves Christ who remains with Christ here in this world, clings to Him with his heart, endures suffering or the cross with Him without complaint, and desires to be inseparably with Him in the age to come. Such a man says from his heart to Christ: *“It is good for me to draw near to God”* [Psalm 72:28].

sections.heading: Love proved by love of neighbor

pairs.en: 6) A sign of love for God is love for one's neighbor. Whoever truly loves God loves his neighbor too. Whoever loves someone who himself loves, loves also what that person loves. Love for God is the source of love for neighbor, yet love for God is recognized by love for neighbor. From this it follows that whoever does not love his neighbor does not love God either, as the apostle teaches: *“If anyone says, 'I love God,' and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?* *And this commandment we have from Him: that he who loves God must love his brother also”* [1 John 4:20–21].

sections.heading: Let love be planted in our hearts

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! Let us repent and turn away from the vanity of the world, and cleanse our hearts through repentance and contrition, that the love of God may dwell within us. *“God is Love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God in him”* [1 John 4:16]. Amen.
